vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: Extremely large input key lengths, theoretically around SIZE_MAX/2 in the disclosed analysis, can wrap the combined temporary-buffer size used by the downstream multibyte comparator before converted bytes are copied.
vulnerability_evidence.bug_type: integer overflow in temporary sort-key buffer sizing
vulnerability_evidence.notes: This is a distinct downstream coreutils-i18n.patch vulnerability in the same reproducibly reconstructed Fedora 22 coreutils-8.23-9.fc22 source state as CVE-2015-4041. The SRPM payload and its RPM signature were not independently downloaded or authenticated. The pre-fix keycompare_mb computes lena + 1 + lenb + 1 without an overflow guard. Our source-level hunk reconstruction finds that the intermediate 8.23-10.fc22 change fixes multibyte expansion but leaves (lena + lenb) * MB_CUR_MAX + 2 overflowable; Fedora commit 4989cfae, package 8.23-11.fc22, adds SIZE_MAX - lenb - 2 < lena and uses xnmalloc. This hunk-level attribution is not a claim that Fedora's changelog separately labeled the two revisions that way. MITRE explicitly assigns the SIZE_MAX/2 issue separately and notes that its arithmetic defect is not specifically caused by multibyte expansion, although the affected downstream function is selected only for a multibyte locale. Pristine upstream 8.23 keycompare contains a parallel unguarded aggregate expression, but keycompare_mb is downstream-only, and the disclosure plus Debian's non-affected status do not support promoting upstream keycompare into this CVE mapping.

vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: Long UTF-8 sort keys processed by the case-folding/translation path in a multibyte locale can expand when wcrtomb emits the towupper result beyond the temporary buffer sized only from input byte lengths.
vulnerability_evidence.bug_type: heap buffer overflow from undersized multibyte conversion buffer
vulnerability_evidence.notes: This is a downstream coreutils-i18n.patch vulnerability, not a defect in pristine GNU Coreutils 8.23. Fedora 22 packaging revision 79d651a2 reproducibly reconstructs the pre-fix coreutils-8.23-9.fc22 source state; the SRPM payload and its RPM signature were not independently downloaded or authenticated. In src/sort.c::keycompare_mb, xmalloc(lena + 1 + lenb + 1) reserves no expansion factor while the wcrtomb(... towupper(...)) case-folding/translation path can emit up to MB_CUR_MAX bytes per input byte. The ignore/filter branch copies bytes and is not an independent expansion source. Fedora commit 8d61fd49 changes the allocation and copy_b offset to multiply by MB_CUR_MAX and advances the package to 8.23-10.fc22. The MITRE assignment distinguishes this multibyte-expansion defect from CVE-2015-4042. LC_ALL=C does not select this downstream multibyte comparator.

vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: A sufficiently long sort input line under -d or -M in a multibyte locale drives downstream i18n comparator lengths into unbounded alloca() stack allocations and can crash sort.
vulnerability_evidence.notes: This is a downstream coreutils-i18n.patch vulnerability, not a defect in pristine GNU Coreutils 8.17. Fedora 18 packaging revision 1b40d50d reproducibly reconstructs coreutils-8.17-7.fc18; its child 8def2175 advances to coreutils-8.17-8.fc18 and applies the SUSE-originated CVE fix. coreutils-8.17-7.fc18.src.rpm is the source-package identity represented by the frozen packaging state; the SRPM payload and its RPM signature were not independently downloaded or authenticated. The source state is reproducibly reconstructed from authenticated GNU Coreutils 8.17 plus immutable Fedora dist-git packaging metadata and frozen patch blobs. In src/sort.c::keycompare_mb, the -d ignore/filter branch allocates lena + 1 + lenb + 1 bytes on the stack. In the independent -M path, keycompare_mb dispatches through getmonth to src/sort.c::getmonth_mb, which allocates len + 1 bytes twice and (len + 1) * sizeof(wchar_t) bytes once on the stack. The fixed patch replaces all four allocations with xmalloc and frees them. Both caller locations are retained because the two disclosed trigger classes reach separate input-sized allocation sites. CWE-20 is the current NVD classification; the concrete consequence is stack exhaustion/stack-based overflow causing denial of service, not the later 2015 heap or integer-overflow defects. Static function-pointer declarations are recorded as evidence but are not promoted into graph edges.

vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: A local attacker able to modify a writable parent directory can substitute a filesystem object after mkdir creates the requested path but before mkdir -m changes permissions through that pathname.
vulnerability_evidence.notes: GNU Coreutils 5.2.1 src/mkdir.c::main creates an ordinary mkdir -m directory and then calls chmod through the pathname. Its -p path calls the historical lib/makepath.c::make_path helper, which independently creates the final directory and performs a pathname chmod when special mode bits require a post-creation change. make_dir only creates and reports state, so it is not promoted. Upstream commit 52893ffd hardens main with descriptor-based chmod_safer; the later a60cc14/76b12f0 redesign replaces the historical helper with make_dir_parents and removes temporarily permissive directory creation. Official 5.97 source still predates that redesign, while v6.0 contains the changes and the open/fchmod-capable dirchownmod implementation also present in v6.1. A later GNU reply names then-current test version 6.1 but does not establish it as the first fixed release. Debian's 6.10-1 package version is downstream evidence, not the upstream fixed version. NVD supplies only its general NVD-CWE-Other classification.

vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: A crafted fixed-string pattern shorter than one eleventh of a large final input buffer that drives grep -F's memchr_kwset search pointer beyond the end pointer.
vulnerability_evidence.notes: Savannah's annotated v2.21 tag peels to the frozen source revision, whose released src/kwset.c contains the vulnerable bmexec_trans implementation. The upstream fix changes bmexec_trans and adds tests/kwset-abuse, explicitly naming grep 2.19 through 2.21 as affected; Savannah ancestry places the fix after v2.21 and before v2.22. NVD assigns CWE-119. Stack callers remain call-path evidence and are not promoted to vulnerable functions.

vulnerability_evidence.attacker_input: A very long searched input line whose length exceeds the historical signed offset and index ranges can trigger narrowing in GNU grep 2.10's matcher and corrupt the returned match bounds.
vulnerability_evidence.bug_type: integer overflow leading to heap-based buffer overflow
vulnerability_evidence.notes: The original oss-security request demonstrates a greater-than-2-GiB searched line and says that this specific problem was fixed by cbbc1a45b9f843c811905c97c90a5d31f8e6c189; the assignment reply gives CVE-2012-5667 to this issue. In GNU grep 2.10, src/dfasearch.c::EGexecute narrows input-line pointer differences and match lengths, allowing an invalid match bound to reach its caller. That is the sole disclosure-supported vulnerable location. lex and the src/main.c functions changed by cbbc1a45 and 8fcf6152 remain in patched_functions as pattern-bound, count, argument-sizing, or propagated hardening provenance, but they are not counted in vulnerability-depth statistics. The reporter separately described 4572ea46 and 8fcf6152 as other patches that might be security relevant; their later appearance in CVE reference lists does not establish every touched function as a CVE location. GNU grep 2.10 predates the long-line fix, 2.11 contains it, and NVD assigns CWE-189. The disclosure-level decision and preserved candidate audit trail are in evidence/CVE-2012-5667.md.
